correctness.rationale: For a height-two bipartite comparability poset, downsets and upsets each number i(G); admissible pairs with both sides nonempty are exactly bipartite-clique subset pairs, counted by i(bipartite complement)-2^a-2^b+1. This gives the stated exact formula. Isolated-side padding yields 2^(k+1)i(G)+Delta with -1<=Delta<2^k, hence floor((c+1)/2^(k+1))=i(G). Adding one disjoint edge preserves height exactly two and multiplies i(G) by 3. Ternary certificates prove membership in #P; finite direct enumeration and independent graph counts passed 682 exhaustive, 240 sample and 130 disjoint-edge checks.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general #P-completeness statement covers arbitrary posets and a greatest-element promise, not the restricted input class height two, and Turing completeness is not equivalent to a one-query extraction. The 2018 source counts structures with a fixed set of minima; the 2025 polynomial imposes a containment condition on the generating upset/downset, not the comparability L<U of a new point. No stronger theorem was identified from the examined material that logically yields height-two hardness.

value.rationale: Height one admits a closed formula, while height exactly two already realizes #P-complete exact finite-parameter type counting. A single-query extraction is a concrete structural transfer rather than a renaming of the unrestricted hardness theorem, and the bipartite-complement identity links model-theoretic one-point extensions to classical combinatorial partition functions.
